name: Vero VR-N76
notes: Vero Telecom VR-N76, programmed over the Benshi BLE/RFCOMM protocol via the emuehlstein/benlink fork (branch n76-support), not CHIRP. There is no CHIRP driver, so no chirp section is declared. Limits are device-reported, not spec-sheet: a live GetDeviceInfo on Eric's unit (2026-09-15, firmware 147) returned region_count 6, channel_count 32, frequency_range_count 5, supports_dmr false, supports_gmrs false, supports_noaa false, supports_vfo false. max_channels 192 is therefore 6 regions x 32 channels, and it is a per-unit figure: the Vero phone app exposes more regions on some units, so a different VR-N76 may legitimately report a larger region_count. Re-read device_info before trusting 192 on a second radio. A region is this radio's zone: channel IDs restart at 0 in every region and a channel only exists inside one region, so codeplugger zones map 1:1 onto regions with no shared global channel pool. max_channel_name_chars 10 is exact, from the wire format: RfCh.name_str is bf_str(10) in benlink protocol/command/rf_ch.py. Bandwidth is a single bit (NARROW/WIDE) mapping to 12.5/25 kHz. Sub-audio is CTCSS 67.0-254.1 Hz or DCS, per RfCh SubAudioMap. UNVERIFIED: the 136-174 / 400-480 band edges are the published dual-band figures, not measured. The device reports 5 frequency ranges but the Benshi protocol exposes only the count, never the edges (there is no freq-range read in benlink, only a use_freq_range_2 settings flag), so the real limits cannot be confirmed over the air and must be checked against the radio display. AM is declared as a valid mode: Eric confirmed 2026-09-16 that this unit receives AM airband (108-137 MHz) despite GetDeviceInfo's supports_gmrs/supports_noaa/etc bits saying nothing about it directly -- those flags describe app-level feature gating, not the RfCh modulation enum, which has always included AM (ModulationType.AM = 1, tx_mod/rx_mod independent fields) per benlink protocol/command/rf_ch.py. The 'Airband' band entry is rx_only: true and every exporter must refuse tx_permitted: true on an AM channel -- there is no FCC/Part 97 authority to transmit on 108-137 MHz from an amateur station, so this is a legal constraint enforced in software, not a hardware one. Untested: AM transmit itself (deliberately never attempted), and the 25 kHz airband channel spacing assumption -- the bandwidth field is a single NARROW/WIDE bit meant for FM deviation and its effect (if any) on AM channels is unverified. DMR is protocol-supported (RfChDMR) but supports_dmr is false on this hardware.
